claim: Meiotic chromosome segregation relies on synapsis and crossover (CO) recombination between homologous chromosomes.
source: Meiotic chromosome segregation relies on synapsis and crossover (CO) recombination between homologous chromosomes.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about meiotic processes.

claim: Failures in chromosome synapsis can trigger a cell cycle delay and/or lead to apoptosis in diverse species.
source: In diverse species, failures in chromosome synapsis can trigger a cell cycle delay and/or lead to apoptosis.
evidence: This is a general statement about meiotic surveillance mechanisms across species, representing established knowledge.

claim: In C. elegans, recruitment of PLK-2 to the synaptonemal complex triggers phosphorylation and inactivation of CHK-2.
source: Here we report that in C. elegans, recruitment of the Polo-like kinase PLK-2 to the synaptonemal complex triggers phosphorylation and inactivation of CHK-2, an early meiotic kinase required for pairing, synapsis, and double-strand break (DSB) induction.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data including in vitro phosphorylation assays, mass spectrometry, and genetic analyses.

claim: CHK-2 is an early meiotic kinase required for pairing, synapsis, and double-strand break (DSB) induction.
source: Here we report that in C. elegans, recruitment of the Polo-like kinase PLK-2 to the synaptonemal complex triggers phosphorylation and inactivation of CHK-2, an early meiotic kinase required for pairing, synapsis, and double-strand break (DSB) induction.
evidence: This is supported by prior literature citations and experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Inactivation of CHK-2 terminates DSB formation and enables CO designation and cell cycle progression.
source: Inactivation of CHK-2 terminates DSB formation and enables CO designation and cell cycle progression.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that CHK-2 depletion leads to earlier CO designation.

claim: A single round of DNA replication at meiotic entry is followed by two nuclear divisions.
source: A single round of DNA replication at meiotic entry is followed by two nuclear divisions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the meiotic cell cycle.

claim: Chiasmata direct bipolar orientation and segregation of homologous chromosomes during Meiosis I together with sister chromatid cohesion.
source: Together with sister chromatid cohesion, chiasmata direct bipolar orientation and segregation of homologous chromosomes during Meiosis I (Hillers et al., 2017; Hunter, 2015; Ur and Corbett, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Synapsis and recombination are monitored by meiotic checkpoints that can delay cell cycle progression and/or lead to apoptosis when these processes are impaired.
source: Synapsis and recombination are monitored by meiotic checkpoints that can delay cell cycle progression and/or lead to apoptosis when these processes are impaired (Subramanian and Hochwagen, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Formation and initial processing of DSBs in C. elegans requires the activity of CHK-2.
source: In C. elegans, formation and initial processing of DSBs requires the activity of CHK-2, a meiosis-specific homolog of the DNA damage transducing kinase Chk2/CHEK2 (MacQueen and Villeneuve, 2001; Oishi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CHK-2 is a meiosis-specific homolog of the DNA damage transducing kinase Chk2/CHEK2.
source: In C. elegans, formation and initial processing of DSBs requires the activity of CHK-2, a meiosis-specific homolog of the DNA damage transducing kinase Chk2/CHEK2 (MacQueen and Villeneuve, 2001; Oishi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CHK-2 is eventually inactivated at mid-pachytene.
source: CHK-2 is eventually inactivated at mid-pachytene; based on cytological markers, this roughly coincides with cessation of DSB formation and the resolution of many intermediates through a 'generic' (as opposed to meiosis-specific) homologous recombination pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations in the manuscript.

claim: CHK-2 inactivation at mid-pachytene roughly coincides with cessation of DSB formation.
source: CHK-2 is eventually inactivated at mid-pachytene; based on cytological markers, this roughly coincides with cessation of DSB formation and the resolution of many intermediates through a 'generic' (as opposed to meiosis-specific) homologous recombination pathway.
evidence: This is based on cytological observations and inference from the data.

claim: A similar mid-prophase transition has been described in budding yeast and mammals.
source: A similar transition during mid-prophase has been described in budding yeast and mammals.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Mid-prophase progression depends on assembly of the synaptonemal complex (SC).
source: In each case, this progression depends on assembly of the synaptonemal complex (SC), a meiosis-specific protein scaffold that assembles between homologous chromosomes (Enguita-Marruedo et al., 2019; Hayashi et al., 2007; Kauppi et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2021; Mu et al., 2020; Murakami et al., 2020; Nadarajan et al., 2017; Thacker et al., 2014; Wojtasz et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The synaptonemal complex is a meiosis-specific protein scaffold that assembles between homologous chromosomes.
source: In each case, this progression depends on assembly of the synaptonemal complex (SC), a meiosis-specific protein scaffold that assembles between homologous chromosomes (Enguita-Marruedo et al., 2019; Hayashi et al., 2007; Kauppi et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2021; Mu et al., 2020; Murakami et al., 2020; Nadarajan et al., 2017; Thacker et al., 2014; Wojtasz et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CHK-2 is inactive in proliferating germline stem cells and becomes active upon meiotic entry.
source: CHK-2 is inactive in proliferating germline stem cells and becomes active upon meiotic entry.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: CHK-2 activation is promoted by targeted degradation of a CHK-2 inhibitor, PPM-1.D/Wip1.
source: The mechanism of activation has not been fully established, but it is promoted by targeted degradation of a CHK-2 inhibitor, PPM-1.D/Wip1 (Baudrimont et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A CHK-2 ortholog in budding yeast, Mek1, undergoes trans-autophosphorylation of its activation loop.
source: Work in budding yeast has shown that a CHK-2 ortholog, Mek1, undergoes trans-autophosphorylation of its activation loop (Carballo et al., 2008; Niu et al., 2007); this mechanism is likely conserved in C. elegans since the activation loop of CHK-2 also contains a CHK-2 consensus phosphorylation motif (R-x-x-S/T) (O'Neill et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The trans-autophosphorylation mechanism is likely conserved in C. elegans CHK-2.
source: Work in budding yeast has shown that a CHK-2 ortholog, Mek1, undergoes trans-autophosphorylation of its activation loop (Carballo et al., 2008; Niu et al., 2007); this mechanism is likely conserved in C. elegans since the activation loop of CHK-2 also contains a CHK-2 consensus phosphorylation motif (R-x-x-S/T) (O'Neill et al., 2002).
evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation and prior knowledge.

claim: CHK-2 contains a forkhead-associated (FHA) domain that recognizes phosphorylated motifs of the consensus (pT-X-X-[I/L/V]).
source: Like all Chk2 homologs, CHK-2 contains a forkhead-associated (FHA) domain and thus recognizes phosphorylated motifs of the consensus (pT-X-X-[I/L/V]) (Durocher and Jackson, 2002; Li et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Mammalian Chk2 undergoes homodimerization through binding of its FHA domain to N-terminal motifs phosphorylated by ATM.
source: While mammalian Chk2 undergoes homodimerization through binding of its FHA domain to N-terminal motifs phosphorylated by ATM (Oliver et al., 2006), the meiosis-specific Mek1 (S. cerevisiae and S. pombe) and CHK-2 (C. elegans) kinases lack this regulatory domain.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The meiosis-specific Mek1 and CHK-2 kinases lack the N-terminal regulatory domain present in mammalian Chk2.
source: While mammalian Chk2 undergoes homodimerization through binding of its FHA domain to N-terminal motifs phosphorylated by ATM (Oliver et al., 2006), the meiosis-specific Mek1 (S. cerevisiae and S. pombe) and CHK-2 (C. elegans) kinases lack this regulatory domain.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and prior knowledge.

claim: Activation of meiotic CHK-2/Mek1 kinases is likely promoted by binding to target motifs on other proteins, resulting in high local concentrations that enable intermolecular trans-phosphorylation.
source: Activation is likely promoted by binding of these kinases to target motifs on other proteins, such as Hop1 in budding yeast (Carballo et al., 2008), resulting in high local concentrations that enable intermolecular trans-phosphorylation.
evidence: This is inferred from prior work and supported by citation.

claim: The Pairing Center proteins HIM-8 and ZIM-1, -2, -3 contain FHA-binding motifs that recruit CHK-2 during early meiotic prophase.
source: In C. elegans, the Pairing Center proteins HIM-8 and ZIM-1, -2, -3 contain FHA-binding motifs that recruit CHK-2 during early meiotic prophase.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: CHK-2 phosphorylates a Polo box interacting motif on Pairing Center proteins, which primes the recruitment of PLK-2.
source: By phosphorylating a Polo box interacting motif on these proteins, CHK-2 primes the recruitment of the Polo-like kinase PLK-2 (Harper et al., 2011; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CHK-2 and PLK-2 at Pairing Centers modify NE proteins including lamin (LMN-1) and the LINC protein SUN-1, which promotes chromosome pairing and synapsis.
source: Together, CHK-2 and PLK-2 at Pairing Centers modify NE proteins including lamin (LMN-1) and the LINC protein SUN-1, which promotes chromosome pairing and synapsis (Link et al., 2018; Penkner et al., 2009; Sato et al., 2009; Woglar et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CHK-2 is required for chromosome pairing as well as for DSB induction.
source: Thus, CHK-2 is required for chromosome pairing as well as for DSB induction.
evidence: This is supported by prior literature and experimental data.

claim: By mid-pachytene, most recombination intermediates disappear, while six 'designated crossover' foci are detected in each nucleus, one per chromosome pair.
source: By mid-pachytene, most of these recombination intermediates disappear, while six 'designated crossover' foci, which show strong localization of the cyclin homolog COSA-1 and other pro-CO factors, are detected in each nucleus, one per chromosome pair (Woglar and Villeneuve, 2018; Yokoo et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature and experimental observations.

claim: Designated crossover foci show strong localization of the cyclin homolog COSA-1 and other pro-CO factors.
source: By mid-pachytene, most of these recombination intermediates disappear, while six 'designated crossover' foci, which show strong localization of the cyclin homolog COSA-1 and other pro-CO factors, are detected in each nucleus, one per chromosome pair (Woglar and Villeneuve, 2018; Yokoo et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Pro-CO factors are thought to prevent non-CO resolution and eventually promote the resolution of late intermediates as COs.
source: Collectively, pro-CO factors are thought to prevent non-CO resolution and eventually promote the resolution of these late intermediates as COs.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge and inference from prior work.

claim: Defects in synapsis or establishment of CO intermediates result in activation of a 'crossover assurance checkpoint' and a delay in cell cycle progression.
source: Defects in synapsis or establishment of CO intermediates result in activation of a 'crossover assurance checkpoint' and a delay in cell cycle progression (reviewed in Yu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Activation of the crossover assurance checkpoint is detected cytologically as an extended region of CHK-2 activity.
source: Activation of the checkpoint is detected cytologically as an extended region of CHK-2 activity.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Defects in synapsis prolong the 'transition zone' (leptotene/zygotene) stage of meiosis, which is characterized by clustering of chromosomes and high CHK-2 activity.
source: Based on nuclear morphology and cytological reporters of CHK-2 activity, defects in synapsis prolong the 'transition zone' (leptotene/zygotene) stage of meiosis, which is characterized by clustering of chromosomes and high CHK-2 activity, while defects in recombination result in a prolonged 'early pachytene' stage, with more dispersed chromosomes and intermediate level of CHK-2 activity (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Defects in recombination result in a prolonged 'early pachytene' stage, with more dispersed chromosomes and intermediate level of CHK-2 activity.
source: Based on nuclear morphology and cytological reporters of CHK-2 activity, defects in synapsis prolong the 'transition zone' (leptotene/zygotene) stage of meiosis, which is characterized by clustering of chromosomes and high CHK-2 activity, while defects in recombination result in a prolonged 'early pachytene' stage, with more dispersed chromosomes and intermediate level of CHK-2 activity (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In mutants competent to form some COs despite defects in synapsis or recombination, the region of nuclei displaying designated CO sites is shifted proximally within the germline.
source: In mutants that are competent to form some COs despite defects in synapsis or recombination, the region of nuclei displaying a limited number of 'designated' CO sites is also shifted proximally within the germline (Kim et al., 2015; Rosu et al., 2013; Stamper et al., 2013; Woglar and Villeneuve, 2018; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Feedback regulation of CHK-2 requires a family of HORMA domain proteins that bind to the chromosome axis.
source: This feedback regulation requires a family of HORMA domain proteins that bind to the chromosome axis (Kim et al., 2015), but how cells detect defects in synapsis or CO intermediates and how CHK-2 activity is prolonged remain unknown.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: CO designation occurs concomitantly with loss of CHK-2 activity.
source: Co-staining of pHIM-8/ZIMs and GFP::COSA-1 confirmed that CO designation occurs concomitantly with loss of CHK-2 activity (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: CHK-2 inactivation and CO designation are both delayed in mutants that activate the CO assurance checkpoint.
source: Since CHK-2 inactivation and CO designation are both delayed in mutants that activate the CO assurance checkpoint (Kim et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2018), we wondered whether CHK-2 activity inhibits CO designation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CHK-2 activity during early meiotic prophase is essential for DSB formation and synapsis.
source: Because CHK-2 activity during early meiotic prophase is essential for DSB formation and synapsis (MacQueen and Villeneuve, 2001; Oishi et al., 2001), and thus for the establishment of recombination intermediates that are prerequisite for CO designation, we exploited the auxin-inducible degradation (AID) system to deplete the CHK-2 protein (Nishimura et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Activity of degron-tagged CHK-2 became undetectable in meiotic nuclei within 3 hr of auxin treatment.
source: Activity of degron-tagged CHK-2 became undetectable in meiotic nuclei within 3 hr of auxin treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Depletion of CHK-2 shifted the appearance of nuclei containing bright COSA-1 foci to a more distal (earlier) position in the germline, indicative of accelerated CO designation and cell cycle progression.
source: Depletion of CHK-2 shifted the appearance of nuclei containing bright COSA-1 foci to a more distal (earlier) position in the germline, indicative of accelerated CO designation and cell cycle progression (Figure 2A, C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, C.

claim: Depletion of CHK-2 restores earlier CO designation in him-8 mutants.
source: We depleted CHK-2 in him-8 and him-5 mutants, which specifically affect synapsis or DSB induction on the X chromosomes, respectively, but do not impair CO formation on autosomes (Hodgkin et al., 1979; Broverman and Meneely, 1994; Phillips et al., 2005; Meneely et al., 2012). In each case, we observed a shift in the appearance of bright COSA-1 foci toward the distal region of meiotic prophase following CHK-2 depletion (Figure 2B, D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: Depletion of CHK-2 restores earlier CO designation in him-5 mutants.
source: We depleted CHK-2 in him-8 and him-5 mutants, which specifically affect synapsis or DSB induction on the X chromosomes, respectively, but do not impair CO formation on autosomes (Hodgkin et al., 1979; Broverman and Meneely, 1994; Phillips et al., 2005; Meneely et al., 2012). In each case, we observed a shift in the appearance of bright COSA-1 foci toward the distal region of meiotic prophase following CHK-2 depletion (Figure 2B, D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–F.

claim: him-8 mutants specifically affect synapsis on the X chromosomes but do not impair CO formation on autosomes.
source: We depleted CHK-2 in him-8 and him-5 mutants, which specifically affect synapsis or DSB induction on the X chromosomes, respectively, but do not impair CO formation on autosomes (Hodgkin et al., 1979; Broverman and Meneely, 1994; Phillips et al., 2005; Meneely et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: him-5 mutants specifically affect DSB induction on the X chromosomes but do not impair CO formation on autosomes.
source: We depleted CHK-2 in him-8 and him-5 mutants, which specifically affect synapsis or DSB induction on the X chromosomes, respectively, but do not impair CO formation on autosomes (Hodgkin et al., 1979; Broverman and Meneely, 1994; Phillips et al., 2005; Meneely et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CHK-2 activity is required to delay CO designation in response to feedback regulation.
source: This result reinforces evidence described above that CHK-2 activity is required to delay CO designation in response to feedback regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing that CHK-2 depletion restores earlier CO designation in checkpoint-activated mutants.

claim: In him-8 mutants, RAD-51 foci were far more abundant in the extended region of CHK-2 activity and persisted even after CHK-2 was depleted.
source: We observed some differences between the two mutants: in him-8 mutants RAD-51 foci were far more abundant in the extended region of CHK-2 activity, and persisted even after CHK-2 was depleted, resulting in the appearance of nuclei with both RAD-51 foci and bright COSA-1 foci.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: In him-5 mutants, RAD-51 foci were sparser and mostly disappeared upon CHK-2 depletion.
source: In contrast, RAD-51 foci were sparser in him-5 and mostly disappeared upon CHK-2 depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: him-8 oocytes are defective in synapsis and arrest at a zygotene-like state with high CHK-2 activity.
source: These differences may reflect the different arrest points of the two mutants: him-8 oocytes are defective in synapsis (Phillips et al., 2005), and thus arrest at a zygotene-like state with high CHK-2 activity, while him-5 mutants are deficient in DSB initiation on the X chromosome (Meneely et al., 2012), and thus arrest at early pachytene with an intermediate level of CHK-2 activity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature and experimental observations.

claim: him-5 mutants are deficient in DSB initiation on the X chromosome and arrest at early pachytene with an intermediate level of CHK-2 activity.
source: These differences may reflect the different arrest points of the two mutants: him-8 oocytes are defective in synapsis (Phillips et al., 2005), and thus arrest at a zygotene-like state with high CHK-2 activity, while him-5 mutants are deficient in DSB initiation on the X chromosome (Meneely et al., 2012), and thus arrest at early pachytene with an intermediate level of CHK-2 activity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature and experimental observations.

claim: The Polo-like kinase Plk1 enables mammalian cells to enter mitosis following DDR activation by phosphorylating the FHA domain of Chk2, which inhibits substrate binding.
source: Prior work on inactivation of DNA damage response (DDR) signaling in proliferating cells revealed that the Polo-like kinase Plk1 enables mammalian cells to enter mitosis following DDR activation by phosphorylating the FHA domain of Chk2, which inhibits substrate binding (van Vugt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: C. elegans expresses multiple homologs of mammalian Plk1, including PLK-1 and PLK-2.
source: C. elegans expresses multiple homologs of mammalian Plk1, including PLK-1, which is essential for mitosis and thus for viability, and PLK-2, which is dispensable for development but plays important roles in meiosis (Chase et al., 2000; Harper et al., 2011; Labella et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: PLK-1 is essential for mitosis and thus for viability.
source: C. elegans expresses multiple homologs of mammalian Plk1, including PLK-1, which is essential for mitosis and thus for viability, and PLK-2, which is dispensable for development but plays important roles in meiosis (Chase et al., 2000; Harper et al., 2011; Labella et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: PLK-2 is dispensable for development but plays important roles in meiosis.
source: C. elegans expresses multiple homologs of mammalian Plk1, including PLK-1, which is essential for mitosis and thus for viability, and PLK-2, which is dispensable for development but plays important roles in meiosis (Chase et al., 2000; Harper et al., 2011; Labella et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in plk-2 perturb pairing and synapsis.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in plk-2 perturb pairing and synapsis, and also cause a pronounced delay in CO designation and subsequent chromosome remodeling during late prophase (Harper et al., 2011; Labella et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in plk-2 cause a pronounced delay in CO designation and subsequent chromosome remodeling during late prophase.
source: Loss-of-function mutations in plk-2 perturb pairing and synapsis, and also cause a pronounced delay in CO designation and subsequent chromosome remodeling during late prophase (Harper et al., 2011; Labella et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Mass spectrometry identified threonine 120 of CHK-2 as an in vitro target of PLK-2.
source: Mass spectrometry identified threonine 120 of CHK-2 as an in vitro target of PLK-2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Threonine 120 of CHK-2 is a highly conserved residue that lies within the FHA substrate recognition domain.
source: This highly conserved residue lies within the FHA substrate recognition domain (Figure 3A, B), close to serine 116, which corresponds to a site phosphorylated by Plk1 in human cells during DNA damage checkpoint adaptation (van Vugt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 3A, B and citation to prior literature.

claim: Serine 116 of CHK-2 corresponds to a site phosphorylated by Plk1 in human cells during DNA damage checkpoint adaptation.
source: This highly conserved residue lies within the FHA substrate recognition domain (Figure 3A, B), close to serine 116, which corresponds to a site phosphorylated by Plk1 in human cells during DNA damage checkpoint adaptation (van Vugt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: S116 and T120 of CHK-2 both conform to a consensus motif for Plk1 substrates.
source: S116 and T120 both conform to a consensus motif for Plk1 substrates (Figure 3A; Santamaria et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3A and citation to prior literature.

claim: CHK-2 is phosphorylated on Thr120 in vivo.
source: Mass spectrometry analyses of the immunoprecipitates revealed that CHK-2 is indeed phosphorylated on Thr120 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Phosphorylation of CHK-2 might lead to its degradation.
source: Based on other evidence (see below) we suspected that phosphorylation of CHK-2 might lead to its degradation.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on experimental observations.

claim: Depletion of proteasome subunit PAS-1 increases the abundance of CHK-2.
source: Under conditions in which PAS-1 was efficiently depleted, CHK-2 was clearly enriched (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Mutation of S116 or T120 to nonphosphorylatable and phosphomimetic residues reduces the abundance of CHK-2 protein.
source: Surprisingly, the abundance of all these mutant CHK-2 proteins was much lower than the wild-type protein; only S116A was detectable (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Mutation of S116 or T120 leads to loss of CHK-2 function.
source: Consistent with the reduced abundance of CHK-2 protein, mutation of these residues led to loss of CHK-2 function: phopsho-HIM-8/ZIMs was not detectable and bivalent formation was defective; only S116A was partially functional (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Mutations of S116 or T120 destabilize CHK-2 in addition to potentially inhibiting substrate binding.
source: These observations suggest that these mutations destabilize CHK-2 in addition to potentially inhibiting substrate binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of reduced protein abundance and loss of function.

claim: Depletion of PLK-2 significantly delayed CHK-2 inactivation and CO designation.
source: Depletion of PLK-2 significantly delayed CHK-2 inactivation and CO designation (Figure 3C, E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, E.

claim: AID-mediated depletion of CHK-2 restored earlier CO designation in plk-2 mutants.
source: Indeed, we found that AID-mediated depletion of CHK-2 restored earlier CO designation in plk-2 mutants (Figure 3D, F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D, F.

claim: PLK-2 is recruited to the SC by binding to a Polo box interacting motif on SYP-1.
source: As the SC assembles, PLK-2 is recruited to this structure by binding to a Polo box interacting motif on SYP-1 (Sato-Carlton et al., 2017; Brandt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Following CO designation at mid-pachytene, PLK-2 activity becomes restricted to the 'short arms' of each bivalent.
source: Following CO designation at mid-pachytene, PLK-2 activity becomes restricted to the 'short arms' of each bivalent (Sato-Carlton et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: syp-1T452A mutants lack the Polo box-binding motif that recruits Polo kinases to the SC.
source: To test this idea, we examined CHK-2 activity in syp-1T452A mutants, which lack the Polo box-binding motif (S-pT-P) that recruits Polo kinases to the SC (Sato-Carlton et al., 2017; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature and data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The syp-1T452A mutation markedly delayed the appearance of bright COSA-1 foci.
source: Consistent with prior analysis, this single-point mutation markedly delayed the appearance of bright COSA-1 foci (Sato-Carlton et al., 2017; Figure 4B, D).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature and experimental data shown in Figure 4B, D.

claim: CHK-2 activity was extended in syp-1T452A mutants.
source: We found that CHK-2 activity was similarly extended in syp-1T452A mutants (Figure 4B, D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B, D.

claim: Depletion of CHK-2 restored earlier CO designation in syp-1T452A mutants.
source: Depletion of CHK-2 restored earlier CO designation in syp-1T452A mutants (Figure 4C, E), as in plk-2 mutants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C, E.

claim: Binding of PLK-2 to the SC is important for downregulation of CHK-2.
source: Thus, binding of PLK-2 to the SC is important for downregulation of CHK-2, and conversely, the delay in CO designation in syp-1T452A mutants is a direct consequence of persistent CHK-2 activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing that syp-1T452A mutants have extended CHK-2 activity and delayed CO designation, which is rescued by CHK-2 depletion.

claim: The delay in CO designation in syp-1T452A mutants is a direct consequence of persistent CHK-2 activity.
source: Thus, binding of PLK-2 to the SC is important for downregulation of CHK-2, and conversely, the delay in CO designation in syp-1T452A mutants is a direct consequence of persistent CHK-2 activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing that CHK-2 depletion rescues the CO designation delay in syp-1T452A mutants.

claim: Compared to PLK-2 depletion alone, CO designation was further delayed when PLK-1 and PLK-2 were both depleted.
source: Compared to PLK-2 depletion alone, CO designation was further delayed when PLK-1 and PLK-2 were both depleted, indicating that PLK-1 can indeed contribute to CHK-2 inactivation during late prophase (Figure 3C, E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: PLK-1 can contribute to CHK-2 inactivation during late prophase.
source: Compared to PLK-2 depletion alone, CO designation was further delayed when PLK-1 and PLK-2 were both depleted, indicating that PLK-1 can indeed contribute to CHK-2 inactivation during late prophase (Figure 3C, E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observation that co-depletion of PLK-1 and PLK-2 causes a greater delay than PLK-2 depletion alone.

claim: CHK-2 was still eventually inactivated in the absence of both PLK-1 and PLK-2.
source: However, CHK-2 was still eventually inactivated in the absence of both paralogs.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: plk-3 mutants showed no apparent meiotic defects.
source: As previously reported (Harper et al., 2011), plk-3 mutants showed no apparent meiotic defects, and we observed no further delay when we combined a plk-3 deletion with depletion of PLK-1 and PLK-2 (data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature and experimental observations.

claim: PLK-3 does not contribute to inactivating CHK-2, even in the absence of PLK-1 and PLK-2.
source: Thus, PLK-3 does not contribute to inactivating CHK-2, even in the absence of PLK-1 and PLK-2.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that plk-3 deletion does not cause additional delay when combined with PLK-1 and PLK-2 depletion.

claim: The ERK kinase MPK-1 promotes pachytene exit.
source: The ERK kinase MPK-1 promotes pachytene exit and has been proposed to be important for CO designation (Church et al., 1995; Hayashi et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2007; Nadarajan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MPK-1 has been proposed to be important for CO designation.
source: The ERK kinase MPK-1 promotes pachytene exit and has been proposed to be important for CO designation (Church et al., 1995; Hayashi et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2007; Nadarajan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MPK-1::AID was undetectable in germ cells following 1 hr of auxin treatment.
source: MPK-1::AID was undetectable in germ cells following 1 hr of auxin treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Depletion of MPK-1 did not cause any apparent delay in CO designation, either alone or in combination with syp-1T452A.
source: Although depletion of MPK-1 led to a disordered appearance of the proximal germline, it did not cause any apparent delay in CO designation, either alone or in combination with syp-1T452A (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B–E.

claim: MPK-1 activity does not play a role in CO designation.
source: We thus conclude that MPK-1 activity does not play a role in CO designation.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observation that MPK-1 depletion does not delay CO designation.

claim: A rise in CDK activity and/or other spatially regulated signals in the proximal gonad may lead to CHK-2 inactivation even when Polo-like kinase activity is absent.
source: We speculate that a rise in CDK activity and/or other spatially regulated signals in the proximal gonad may lead to CHK-2 inactivation even when Polo-like kinase activity is absent.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation that CHK-2 is eventually inactivated even without PLK-1 and PLK-2.

claim: CHK-2 is normally inactivated at mid-pachytene through the recruitment of PLK-2 to the SC and the formation of CO precursors.
source: In summary, we find that CHK-2 activity is required to inhibit CO designation. CHK-2 is normally inactivated at mid-pachytene through the recruitment of PLK-2 to the SC and the formation of CO precursors, but delays in synapsis prevent the activation of PLK-2 and thereby prolong CHK-2 activity.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: Delays in synapsis prevent the activation of PLK-2 and thereby prolong CHK-2 activity.
source: In summary, we find that CHK-2 activity is required to inhibit CO designation. CHK-2 is normally inactivated at mid-pachytene through the recruitment of PLK-2 to the SC and the formation of CO precursors, but delays in synapsis prevent the activation of PLK-2 and thereby prolong CHK-2 activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: Delays in the establishment of CO intermediates also prolong CHK-2 activity.
source: Notably, delays in the establishment of CO intermediates also prolong CHK-2 activity, and thus full activation of PLK-2 may depend on the formation of CO intermediates on all chromosomes.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Full activation of PLK-2 may depend on the formation of CO intermediates on all chromosomes.
source: Notably, delays in the establishment of CO intermediates also prolong CHK-2 activity, and thus full activation of PLK-2 may depend on the formation of CO intermediates on all chromosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that delays in CO intermediate formation prolong CHK-2 activity.

claim: PLK-2-dependent phosphorylation of the central region protein SYP-4 increases markedly starting at mid-pachytene, concomitant with CO designation.
source: Consistent with this idea, PLK-2-dependent phosphorylation of the central region protein SYP-4 (Nadarajan et al., 2017) increase markedly starting at mid-pachytene, concomitant with CO designation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: PLK-2 appears to associate with designated CO sites even when it cannot be recruited to the SC.
source: How the formation of CO precursors promotes PLK-2 activity remains unclear, but the kinase does appear to associate with designated CO sites even when it cannot be recruited to the SC (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The data support the idea that PLK-2 directly regulates CHK-2 via inhibitory phosphorylation.
source: Our data support the idea that PLK-2 directly regulates CHK-2 via inhibitory phosphorylation, but do not rule out the possibility that recruitment of PLK-2 to the SC leads indirectly to CHK-2 inactivation.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing PLK-2 phosphorylates CHK-2 in vitro and in vivo.

claim: CHK-2 inactivation is reversible through mid-pachytene.
source: A recent study reported that CHK-2 inactivation is reversible through mid-pachytene (Castellano-Pozo et al., 2020), consistent with the idea that it occurs through phosphorylation, which can be reversed by phosphatase activity (Kar and Hochwagen, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Phosphorylated CHK-2 may be degraded after mid-pachytene, resulting in irreversible inactivation.
source: We speculate that phosphorylated CHK-2 may be degraded after mid-pachytene, resulting in irreversible inactivation.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental observations.

claim: Both CHK-2 and PLK-2 are active during leptotene/zygotene, when both kinases are bound to Pairing Centers.
source: Intriguingly, both CHK-2 and PLK-2 are active during leptotene/zygotene, when both kinases are bound to Pairing Centers (Kim et al., 2015; Link et al., 2018; Penkner et al., 2009; Sato et al., 2009; Woglar et al., 2013), implying that in this context PLK-2 does not inactivate CHK-2.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In the context of Pairing Centers during leptotene/zygotene, PLK-2 does not inactivate CHK-2.
source: Intriguingly, both CHK-2 and PLK-2 are active during leptotene/zygotene, when both kinases are bound to Pairing Centers (Kim et al., 2015; Link et al., 2018; Penkner et al., 2009; Sato et al., 2009; Woglar et al., 2013), implying that in this context PLK-2 does not inactivate CHK-2.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both kinases are active simultaneously at Pairing Centers.

claim: The configuration of CHK-2 and PLK-2 recruitment motifs on the Pairing Center proteins may make the target site(s) in the FHA domain of CHK-2 inaccessible to the active site of PLK-2.
source: We speculate that the configuration of CHK-2 and PLK-2 recruitment motifs on the Pairing Center proteins may make the target site(s) in the FHA domain of CHK-2 inaccessible to the active site of PLK-2.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning to explain why PLK-2 does not inactivate CHK-2 at Pairing Centers.

claim: The activity of CHK-2 in early prophase depends on a heterodimeric complex of HAL-2 and HAL-3, which is a meiotic regulator of PLK-2 activity.
source: However, the activity of CHK-2 in early prophase also depends on an enigmatic meiotic regulator of PLK-2 activity, a heterodimeric complex of HAL-2 and HAL-3 (Roelens et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: HAL-2/HAL-3 may inhibit or antagonize phosphorylation of CHK-2.
source: This may inhibit or antagonize phosphorylation of CHK-2.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about the role of HAL-2/HAL-3.

claim: In C. elegans, synapsis can occur normally in the absence of DSBs or recombination intermediates.
source: In C. elegans, synapsis can occur normally in the absence of DSBs or recombination intermediates (Dernburg et al., 1998), and meiocytes surveil both synapsis and CO precursors to ensure chiasma formation and faithful segregation (reviewed by ).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Meiocytes surveil both synapsis and CO precursors to ensure chiasma formation and faithful segregation.
source: In C. elegans, synapsis can occur normally in the absence of DSBs or recombination intermediates (Dernburg et al., 1998), and meiocytes surveil both synapsis and CO precursors to ensure chiasma formation and faithful segregation (reviewed by ).
evidence: This is established knowledge about meiotic surveillance mechanisms.

claim: In organisms where synapsis depends on the stabilization of interhomolog joint molecules through the 'ZMM' pathway, cells may monitor synapsis as a proxy for the presence of CO-competent intermediates.
source: In organisms where synapsis depends on the stabilization of interhomolog joint molecules through the 'ZMM' pathway (Pyatnitskaya et al., 2019), cells may monitor synapsis as a proxy for the presence of CO-competent intermediates.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning about surveillance mechanisms in other organisms.

claim: SC assembly is essential for the surveillance of CO formation.
source: However, in either case, SC assembly is essential for the surveillance.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental findings.

claim: In mouse spermatocytes, PLK-1 localizes along SCs and promotes pachytene exit.
source: In mouse spermatocytes, PLK-1 localizes along SCs and promotes pachytene exit (Jordan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Similar mechanisms may coordinate synapsis with meiotic progression in other organisms.
source: Thus, similar mechanisms may coordinate synapsis with meiotic progression in other organisms.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the findings in C. elegans and mice.

claim: Cells exit proliferation and enter meiosis in the distal 'arms' of the C. elegans gonad and move proximally toward the spermatheca and uterus at a velocity of about one cell row per hour.
source: Cells exit proliferation and enter meiosis in the distal 'arms' of the gonad and move proximally toward the spermatheca and uterus at a velocity of about one cell row per hour (Deshong et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Homolog pairing and synapsis and double-strand break (DSB) induction normally occur during the first few hours following meiotic entry, in the 'transition zone' region corresponding to leptotene and zygotene.
source: Homolog pairing and synapsis and double-strand break (DSB) induction normally occur during the first few hours following meiotic entry, in the 'transition zone' region corresponding to leptotene and zygotene.
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans meiosis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: DSBs are processed to form recombination intermediates, which increase in abundance during early pachytene.
source: DSBs are then processed to form recombination intermediates, which increase in abundance during early pachytene.
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans meiosis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: At mid-pachytene, a transition occurs that leads to disappearance of most intermediates.
source: At mid-pachytene, a transition occurs that leads to disappearance of most intermediates.
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans meiosis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: One recombination intermediate on each pair of chromosomes becomes 'designated' as an eventual crossover site.
source: One recombination intermediate on each pair of chromosomes becomes 'designated' as an eventual crossover site.
evidence: This is established knowledge about C. elegans meiosis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Bright GFP::COSA-1 foci are detected following inactivation of CHK-2.
source: Bright GFP::COSA-1 foci are detected following inactivation of CHK-2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Accumulation of pro-CO proteins can be stratified into three stages: an early stage with high CHK-2 activity and variable numbers of dim GFP::COSA-1; an intermediate stage with brighter and more abundant GFP::COSA-1 foci, and a post-designation stage, with a single CO-designated site per chromosome pair marked by bright GFP::COSA-1 fluorescence.
source: Accumulation of pro-CO proteins can be stratified into three stages: an early stage with high CHK-2 activity and variable numbers of dim GFP::COSA-1; an intermediate stage with brighter and more abundant GFP::COSA-1 foci, and a post-designation stage, with a single CO-designated site per chromosome pair marked by bright GFP::COSA-1 fluorescence.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The intensity of GFP::COSA-1 foci remains fairly constant throughout the post-designation stage.
source: The intensity of GFP::COSA-1 foci remains fairly constant throughout this last stage.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The appearance of bright COSA-1 foci is used as a proxy for crossover designation and the mid-pachytene cell cycle transition.
source: In this work, we use the appearance of bright COSA-1 foci as a proxy for crossover designation and the mid-pachytene cell cycle transition.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about how the authors interpret their data.

claim: PLK-2 localizes to pairing centers in leptotene/zygotene nuclei but fails to localize to SC in pachytene nuclei in syp-1T452A mutants.
source: PLK-2 localized to pairing centers in leptotene/zygotene nuclei but failed to localize to SC in pachytene nuclei in syp-1T452A mutants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.
